parsed_output.analysis: The model correctly captures most of the specification: HumanDriving is a simple state, Autonomous is a compound state with sub-states, the initial transition goes to HumanDriving on Power On, and the front_distance > 10 trigger moves the system into Autonomous. Two non-conformances remain: the exit-from-Autonomous transition is structurally and logically misplaced, and the Power Off event is not handled from the Autonomous state.

issues.issue: The transition to HumanDriving is placed on the compound Autonomous state with the guard `human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed || in (AutoFinal)`. The specification says the transition to human driving mode occurs when a human steering command or brake press is received while in the AutoFinal sub-state. This has two problems: (1) the transition should originate from the AutoFinal sub-state itself, not from the parent compound state, because it is only valid when the system is in that sub-state; (2) the use of `||` (OR) between all three conditions means the transition would fire on being in AutoFinal alone, with no input event, which is not what the specification intends. The correct model would be a transition from AutoFinal to HumanDriving (or outside) triggered by `human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed`.
issues.reason: The specification states the transition is conditioned on being in AutoFinal AND receiving one of the inputs. The model conflates the source-state constraint into a guard and uses the wrong logical operator, changing the behavior.

issues.issue: The specification says 'when power off, it will transit to final state' without restricting this to the HumanDriving mode only. The model defines a Power Off transition only from HumanDriving to the final pseudo-state. There is no corresponding Power Off transition from the Autonomous state (or its sub-states), meaning if power is turned off while in autonomous mode, the state machine has no defined behavior.
issues.reason: A power-off event should be handleable from any active state; the model omits it for the Autonomous sub-machine, leaving an undefined transition that the specification implies should exist.

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] --> HumanDriving : Power On
HumanDriving : Human Driving Mode

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : front_distance > 10
state Autonomous {
[*] --> AutoInitial : Enter Autonomous Mode
AutoInitial --> AutoFinal : Auto Process Complete
AutoFinal : Auto Final State
}

Autonomous --> HumanDriving : human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed || in (AutoFinal)
HumanDriving --> [*] : Power Off
@enduml
